chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Sulaiman, from 'Uthman ibn Aslam, from Muawiya ad-Duhani, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, what is the interpretation of this hadith that I heard from you?' He said: 'And what is it?' I said: '(It is) the believer sees through the light of Allah.' He said: 'O Muawiya, indeed Allah created the believers from His light, dyed them in His mercy, and took a covenant from them for our Wilayah (guardianship) based on their knowledge of Him, on the day He made Himself known to them. Thus, the believer is the brother of the believer in terms of his father and mother: his father is the Light and his mother is the Mercy. He only sees by that Light from which he was created.'

key_terms.الرَّحْمَةُ: The Mercy (divine attribute in which believers are 'dyed' or immersed)
key_terms.النُّورُ: The Light (divine attribute/essence from which believers are created)
key_terms.مَعْرِفَتُهُ: Knowledge of Him (recognition of God, the basis of the covenant)
key_terms.مِيثَاقٌ: Covenant (the divine pledge taken from believers)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual origin and nature of the believer's light according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the metaphysical origin of the believer, linking their spiritual perception directly to the divine Light (Nur) from which they were created, and by extension the Ahl al-Bayt, are derived. This narration underscores the concept of 'spiritual kinship' (Ukhuwwah), where the covenant of Imamate is rooted in a shared ontological substance of Light and Mercy, distinguishing the believer's inner sight from mere physical vision. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the luminous nature of the faithful as a manifestation of divine attributes.
